base_contract.archetype_rationale: Mastercard supplies interoperable payment processing and related services without issuing account-holder credit. Shared acceptance, data and distribution support incremental earnings without proportionate physical capital. Compounding remains conditional on customer incentives, replacement technology, acquisition payback and settlement funding. Rising earnings alongside falling recent operating cash flow contradict effortless cash compounding.
base_contract.framework_rationale: A consolidated parent-equity operating DCF captures the interdependent network and services while charging customer capital, acquisitions, compensation, financing and liquidity. The revised model pays existing notes during their maturity years, reduces interest as principal retires and reaches a debt-free continuation after the final existing maturity. It requires neither perpetual refinancing nor premature prefunding of every maturity.

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: The strongest alternative separates network, services and investments. Both filings describe shared customers, data and distribution, and Mastercard reports one Payment Solutions segment. Separate distributable earnings and independent investment requirements are not established; additive franchise valuations would overlap.

Settlement guarantees create material funding risk, but Mastercard does not issue cards or extend account-holder credit. Deposit-funded lending and regulatory lending-book capital do not describe its principal earning mechanism.
Software, customer incentives and acquired relationships support continuing operations. Their book values do not establish independent recoveries, and liquidation would impair the operating earnings.

base_contract.horizon_rationale: Retain the complete November-to-October funding projection through the March 2051 final existing note maturity. This is the contractual audit horizon, not the assumed ownership period or competitive runway. All scheduled principal, declining interest, investment, liquidity and shareholder distributions remain projected through year 25. Elevated growth and its fade are separately estimated. The compiler transfers the remaining reconciled claim at the seven-year holding date without deleting subsequent obligations or adding a duplicate exit.

component_inventory.rationale: Consumer and commercial payments, switching, security, authentication, insights, gateway, account-based capabilities and open finance share a consolidated valuation.

Existing acquisitions remain consolidated. Approximate acquired revenue of USD 324.96 million, derived from the annual services acquisition bridge, now bounds the owner-profit calibration. Estimated acquired owner earnings are USD 64.992–129.984 million with no unquantified synergies, against complete USD 2,511 million consideration. Forward purchases precede contributions by one year. The failed-payback test preserves purchase cash and BVNK contingent consideration; goodwill receives no separate recovery.

Customer incentives, receivables, deferred revenue and accruals support consolidated operations. The numerical cash recast precedes additional customer capital; incentives already deducted in net revenue are not deducted again as revenue expense. Forward capital uses the same attributed-profit boundary as historical incremental returns, with a separate customer-capital floor and rising operating buffer. Actual revenue growth is reduced when annual internal resources cannot finance deployment. Contraction releases no existing customer assets.

Latest unrestricted cash starts liquidity after estimated subsequent consumption. Current investments of USD 317 million and equity investments of USD 1,671 million receive no emergency-liquidity credit or separate realization. Ordinary portfolio income remains consolidated.

Restricted cash of USD 564 million and customer deposits of USD 2,231 million are excluded from usable cash. Settlement balances remain operational. Post-mitigation exposure supplies a stress denominator, not an asset recovery or maximum legal obligation.

Latest carrying debt of USD 23,938 million reconciles to gross principal of USD 24,081 million through discounts, costs and hedge adjustments. Preserve every gross maturity and declining-interest node through March 2051. Each year-end reserves only the following year's scheduled principal alongside operating liquidity, protecting early-year payments without prefunding all later notes. Annual expansion is capped before these requirements or distributions. Emergency credit remains conditional, capped, priced and repaid by year 3; undrawn capacity is never counted as borrowed cash.

Ordinary legal expense remains in earning power. Additional legal demands and customer failures enter an early creditor waterfall. Fee restrictions affect growth, margins and customer capital. Recorded accruals and settlement-sharing percentages establish no universal loss cap.

Ordinary taxes, leases, sponsorships and licensing costs remain charged. A recurring cash reserve covers nonparent and residual financing payments. Negative minority equity, tax assets and pension surplus create no separate shareholder proceeds.
The November dividend belongs to October 9 record holders. Its payment precedes prospective distributions and is not credited to the newly acquired claim.

The verified quarterly diluted denominator covers participating common classes and existing awards. Economic compensation funding is embedded once in normalized owner earnings. Pro-rata cash distributions and constant shares avoid free repurchase accretion.
Mastercard does not issue cards or extend account-holder credit. Controlled payment entities remain consolidated; settlement guarantees are modeled without inventing a captive lending book.

assumptions.rationale: October repurchases consumed USD 648 million. Retain an additional allowance for net subsequent movements without crediting unknown receipts; separately fund November obligations.
assumptions.counterevidence: Operating receipts may offset purchases; further spending may exceed the allowance.
assumptions.falsifier: Comparable subsequent net consumption falls outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Next cash and capital-return reconciliation.

assumptions.rationale: Desired installed-business nominal growth is -10%, 11% and 14%, before the separate forward acquisition contribution and subject to executable internal funding. Aggregate net revenue grew 12.23% in 2024 and 16.42% in 2025. Current nine-month currency-neutral network growth of 9% and services growth of 18%, weighted by their approximately 59%/41% revenue mix, imply about 12.7%. Base discounts this measured mix for slower activity and renewal concessions; high permits durable services distribution. Low combines spending contraction, weaker cross-border mix and program losses.
assumptions.counterevidence: Recent services growth and operating leverage support greater persistence. Conversely, current currency-neutral incentives grew 19% against network revenue growth of 9%; third-quarter local cross-border growth slowed to 11% from 15% and switched-transaction growth to 9% from 10%.
assumptions.falsifier: Comparable installed-business growth persistently lies outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Quarterly results, major renewals or routing intervention.

assumptions.rationale: Desired installed growth remains near the measured recent network/services mix in base and high, with actual growth limited by internally available capital. The low recovery remains incomplete after the initial contraction. Recent aggregate revenue growth of 12.23% and 16.42% supports persistence; incentives growing faster than net network revenue warrant moderation rather than extrapolating gross assessments.
assumptions.counterevidence: Recovery could accelerate, or substitution could prevent it.
assumptions.falsifier: Recovering activity fails to restore positive net revenue after incentives.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual results and post-downturn operating metrics.

assumptions.rationale: Desired installed growth of 10% and 13% retains adoption and shared services distribution close to the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral mix. The downside recovers slowly with lasting margin concessions. Annual funding limits can reduce achieved growth while preserving maintenance, renewal expense, contractual payments and operating liquidity.
assumptions.counterevidence: Services may sustain faster growth; fee intervention could cause contraction.
assumptions.falsifier: Preserving activity requires concessions that eliminate growth.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual competitive review or material fee restrictions.

assumptions.rationale: Start subsequent desired installed growth at 2%, 10% and 13%. Base and high retain substantial adoption/services persistence relative to 2024–2025 aggregate net revenue growth of 12.23%–16.42% and the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral network/services mix. Long customer contracts, shared acceptance and distribution support opportunity, while variable consideration guarantees neither volumes nor renewal economics. Actual growth remains subject to each year's funded deployment ceiling.
assumptions.counterevidence: Renewal concessions may end profitable deployment sooner; distribution may persist longer.
assumptions.falsifier: Renewals consume capital without subsequent owner-cash gains.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual customer economics and substitute-rail review.

assumptions.rationale: Reduce desired installed growth by two percentage points annually in low, 0.6 points in base and 0.4 points in high, subject to the mature-growth floor. Base reaches mature growth around explicit year 18; high still grows approximately 4.6% in year 25. This materially distinguishes rapid erosion from durable distribution. Competitive mechanisms are issuer concessions, local routing, account-based substitutes and services-market saturation; the funding horizon does not establish the fade.
assumptions.counterevidence: Net revenue grew 12.23% and 16.42% in 2024 and 2025. A cash proxy after physical purchases, capitalized software, SBC and customer-deposit inflows rose from USD 10,155 million in 2023 to USD 13,031 million in 2024 and USD 15,589 million in 2025, approximately 28.3% and 19.6%. These outcomes oppose abrupt assumed maturity, but include timing, installed pricing and operating leverage rather than proving marginal investment returns. Latest nine-month OCF declined despite earnings growth.
assumptions.falsifier: Renewal economics deteriorate faster than the stressed fade or remain durable across repeated renewals.
assumptions.review_trigger: Major renewals, routing changes or sustained service slowdown.

assumptions.rationale: After elevated growth fades, nominal installed-business growth is modest. Prices, payment amounts, wages, replacement costs and customer funding remain linked; no separate inflation uplift is added.
assumptions.counterevidence: Digital adoption may persist faster; regulation or substitution could prevent growth.
assumptions.falsifier: Mature growth requires inadequate maintenance, rising leverage or persistently declining customer returns.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual pricing, costs and payment-rail review.

assumptions.rationale: Continuation after the last existing debt maturity grows no faster than mature economics. Downside mature owner earnings are flat at realization despite modest preceding recovery. Growth requires funded incremental equity.
assumptions.counterevidence: The franchise could persist longer or deteriorate outright.
assumptions.falsifier: Mature earnings cannot grow within the modeled investment requirement.
assumptions.review_trigger: Every annual capital-deployment and competitive review.

assumptions.rationale: After-tax accounting earnings margin before existing debt interest, with ordinary litigation, depreciation and SBC still charged. Reconciled trailing income plus after-tax interest is about 48.8% of revenue. Base discounts tax benefits and grants; downside imposes lasting concessions and operating deleverage.
assumptions.counterevidence: Recent margins improved; incentives and fee intervention could overwhelm downside profitability.
assumptions.falsifier: Comparable after-tax prefinancing margins persist outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual tax, government-grant, incentive and operating-cost disclosures; also review when the paired fiscal-2027 revenue/OCF commitments imply a different owner margin.

assumptions.rationale: Reconstruct trailing reported interest expense from USD 722 million annual expense plus USD 653 million current nine-month expense less USD 563 million comparative expense. Use this solely to reconcile the reported baseline before forecasting retiring debt separately.
assumptions.counterevidence: Accrual expense differs from cash interest and does not annualize the latest debt mix.
assumptions.falsifier: A restatement changes the selected expenses or their reporting periods.
assumptions.review_trigger: Restatement or annual interest reconciliation.

assumptions.rationale: Use a normalized marginal tax rate for interest adjustments, above recent effective rates affected by discrete benefits. Ordinary operating taxes remain in the earnings margin.
assumptions.counterevidence: Geographic mix and deductibility limits may alter realized shields.
assumptions.falsifier: Interest deductions are persistently unavailable or the marginal rate lies outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Tax-law changes, financing stress or annual tax disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Retain a numerical recast of USD 1,241 million: trailing prepaid outflows 5,137 less incentive amortization 2,602 less accrued-expense inflows 2,838 less customer-deposit inflows 193 plus net settlement outflows 23 plus litigation-liability outflows 675 plus receivable outflows 1,039, all in USD millions. This recasts identified timing and capital movements before separately funding incremental customer capital; ordinary incentive amortization, renewal economics and legal expense remain in reported net earnings. Mixed classifications justify the -1,500 to +2,000 million bounds, jointly tested with conversion and customer funding.
assumptions.counterevidence: Prepaid movements include ordinary renewals, and other assets may contain additional incentive funding.
assumptions.falsifier: Consistent classification produces a recast outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual cash-flow and incentive disclosures; jointly stress lower recast and greater customer funding.

assumptions.rationale: Retain 92%, 98% and 102% persistence of numerically reconstructed prefinancing conversion. Current nine-month OCF fell while net income rose, whereas the 2023–2025 cash proxy after physical/software spending, SBC and customer-deposit inflows improved materially. These competing observations support bounded conversion rather than treating all weak cash as deterioration or all incentive payments as investment. The renewal stress now reduces achieved organic growth when the joint capital requirement exceeds internal resources.
assumptions.counterevidence: Conversion may recover more strongly or stay depressed despite earnings growth.
assumptions.falsifier: Comparable annual cash after consistent customer-funding treatment falls outside the implied range.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual OCF commitment and renewal reconciliation.

assumptions.rationale: Trailing physical purchases and software capitalization total about USD 1,431 million. Revenue-linked replacement and resilience spending is embedded in owner earnings; expansion software and equipment belong to separately funded organic deployment. Expensed development remains charged.
assumptions.counterevidence: The split is unreported and resilience obligations may increase replacement costs.
assumptions.falsifier: Maintaining service quality requires replacement spending above the upper bound.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual capital disclosures, outages or resilience requirements.

assumptions.rationale: Embed economic compensation funding above trailing SBC intensity once. Reported cash conversion adds back noncash SBC; the funding deduction supports cash-equivalent compensation or funded participation neutralization. Constant shares receive no repurchase benefit.
assumptions.counterevidence: Grant-date expense differs from realized compensation and participation-neutralization costs.
assumptions.falsifier: Preserving participation requires funding above the bound or dilution persists despite it.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual grants, vesting, withholding and common-share activity.

assumptions.rationale: Translate the reported USD 2,094 million annual net-income increment into a bounded maintenance-adjusted owner-earnings proxy. Annual physical and software spending was USD 1,215 million against USD 1,143 million depreciation and amortization in 2025; accounting earnings are an approximate incremental numerator, not measured marginal cash returns.
assumptions.counterevidence: Acquired amortization, expensed intangibles, tax changes and grants complicate the translation.
assumptions.falsifier: A consistent maintenance and tax reconciliation changes the owner increment beyond the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual cash, amortization, tax and acquisition disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Attribute 40%, 55% and 70% of the nonacquired owner-earnings increment to newly funded organic capital; the remainder reflects installed-network activity, pricing, operating leverage and older investments. After the corrected acquisition contribution, attributed organic earnings are approximately USD 728 million, USD 1,098 million and USD 1,521 million. Apply the identical attribution to forward incremental earnings before dividing by the calibrated return. Customer funding and incremental operating liquidity remain independent floors.
assumptions.counterevidence: Investment lags and expensed development prevent precise attribution.
assumptions.falsifier: Subsequent owner cash fails to follow cumulative funded deployment.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual cumulative customer, expansion and liquidity-capital review.

assumptions.rationale: During 2025, incentive assets increased USD 1,997 million and receivables USD 836 million. The USD 4,400 million, USD 3,700 million and USD 3,400 million capital estimates also allow expansion and operating-liquidity deployment, excluding acquisitions and maintenance already charged. With corrected acquisition attribution, incremental organic returns are approximately 16.6%, 29.7% and 44.7%. These are uncertain earnings/capital estimates with investment lags, not book ROE. Forward funding applies the same attributed-profit boundary; complete continuation returns include installed gains and all funded capital.
assumptions.counterevidence: Balances include currency, amortization and timing; earnings may arise from older vintages.
assumptions.falsifier: Consistent deployment exceeds the bounds without proportionate later earnings.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual investment and owner-cash reconciliation.

assumptions.rationale: Retain USD 1,300 million of annual prospective acquisitions against USD 2,511 million spent in 2024, none in 2025 and USD 1,372 million in the latest nine months. Purchases remain fully charged even when payback fails. Their estimated payoff is now calibrated to disclosed acquired revenue and a bounded owner margin, producing returns below the equity hurdle rather than assuming purchased compounding. Organic expansion is rationed before contractual funding, the acquisition budget or already embedded maintenance is compromised.
assumptions.counterevidence: Purchases are discretionary and lumpy; longer integration or larger transactions may be necessary.
assumptions.falsifier: Multi-year spending exceeds the bounds without subsequent modeled owner earnings.
assumptions.review_trigger: Material acquisitions and annual capital allocation.

assumptions.rationale: Forward purchases earn the revised acquired-revenue-based return after a one-year integration delay. A zero-payoff test preserves all purchases and BVNK contingent consideration while removing acquired revenue and owner earnings. This fixed one-year lag is a judgment to monitor, not proof of achieved cohort returns; margins include ordinary integration costs and no synergy uplift.
assumptions.counterevidence: Integration may take longer or never achieve an adequate return.
assumptions.falsifier: Post-integration contributions fail to match the calibrated return.
assumptions.review_trigger: Integration disclosures, impairments or material service underperformance.

assumptions.rationale: Latest incentive assets increased USD 1,223 million and receivables USD 649 million against comparable nine-month revenue growth of USD 3,497 million. Fund customer capital against positive installed growth and acquired revenue. This floors organic deployment; contraction releases no existing assets.
assumptions.counterevidence: Amortization, translation and renewals complicate the relation between balances and new revenue.
assumptions.falsifier: Incremental and renewal funding exceeds the upper bound or fails to generate later cash.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual incentive, receivable and OCF commitments.

assumptions.rationale: Fund the full disclosed possible contingent consideration in year 1 without separate synergy proceeds. This bound applies only to that consideration.
assumptions.counterevidence: Payment depends on performance and may be smaller or later.
assumptions.falsifier: Final accounting establishes different consideration or timing.
assumptions.review_trigger: Next acquisition and contingent-consideration disclosure.

assumptions.rationale: Embed a recurring cash allowance above reported annual and recent nine-month other-financing outflows for nonparent and residual claims. Ordinary taxes, leases and sponsorship expense remain charged and are not deducted again.
assumptions.counterevidence: Other financing is not a pure minority measure; negative minority equity does not cap obligations.
assumptions.falsifier: Recurring outside payments exceed the bounds or material redemption rights emerge.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual minority, financing and acquisition disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Additional cash is separate from ordinary legal expense. Block and Intuit seek aggregate single damages above USD 5 billion, alongside European and UK matters. Downside combines adverse outcomes and accelerated collection. Immediate collection is a stress timing judgment; no tax or indemnity recovery is credited.
assumptions.counterevidence: Claims are contested and several matters have settled; damages sought are not expected payments.
assumptions.falsifier: Binding outcomes establish amounts or timing outside the bounds; these bounds are not a liability ceiling.
assumptions.review_trigger: November hearing, Block and Intuit developments, UK appeals or substantial new claims.

assumptions.rationale: Apply immediate net cash severity to post-mitigation exposure. Downside correlates customer failures with operating weakness. Annual receipts cannot fund a demand due within days.
assumptions.counterevidence: Historical losses are low and recoveries may reduce payments; expanded Brazilian guarantees can increase exposure.
assumptions.falsifier: Failures or changed guarantees imply severity outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Bank distress, settlement failures, collateral changes or Brazil implementation.

assumptions.rationale: Timely access rests on the undrawn commitment, permitted settlement-failure use, covenant compliance and November 2030 expiry. Access is discrete; lender performance, representations or default conditions can prevent timely drawing. Commercial paper adds no separate capacity.
assumptions.counterevidence: Commitment supports availability, but correlated banking disruption can delay funding.
assumptions.falsifier: A valid timely draw is refused or incompatible restrictions are disclosed.
assumptions.review_trigger: Facility amendments, covenant events, lender distress or settlement failures.

assumptions.rationale: After-tax emergency funding costs exceed ordinary fixed-note costs because facility margins depend on ratings and prevailing rates. Charge a full year on opening drawings before repayment.
assumptions.counterevidence: Repayment may be faster; stressed pricing or unavailable tax benefits may increase cost.
assumptions.falsifier: Executable after-tax funding cost falls outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Drawing, rating change, rate reset or tax restriction.

assumptions.rationale: Charge an additional cash financing and enforcement allowance on early unpaid demands until their modeled year-1 payment. This is a stress cost estimate, not an asserted contractual penalty or legal cap. Existing common owners receive nothing after the early failure.
assumptions.counterevidence: Actual default and enforcement costs may differ and restructuring may be slower.
assumptions.falsifier: Binding terms or proceedings imply larger costs or delayed payment beyond the funded path.
assumptions.review_trigger: Any missed demand, default notice or restructuring.

assumptions.rationale: Retain an operating cash target based on half the latest unrestricted cash, rising with achieved revenue and never automatically declining with contraction. In addition, each year-end retains the following holding year's scheduled principal so early-year maturities do not depend on that year's unearned receipts. Only this next-year amount is reserved; later principal remains on its contractual schedule. Organic growth is capped annually after these requirements, acquisitions and financing costs; distributions remain residual. The operating ratio is an underwriting target, not a disclosed regulatory minimum.
assumptions.counterevidence: Daily requirements may be greater or stable operations may need less.
assumptions.falsifier: Operations require cash above the bound without accessible funding.
assumptions.review_trigger: Settlement stress, regulatory changes or liquidity disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Approximate cash coupon cost on outstanding principal, informed by the disclosed note coupons, limited floating exposure and the latest interest burden. Unlike perpetual embedded interest, this charge falls with contractual principal retirement. A joint test raises the coupon proxy and removes the tax shield.
assumptions.counterevidence: Maturing low-coupon notes change the weighted mix, and fixed coupons do not all reprice together.
assumptions.falsifier: The actual surviving-note coupon burden falls outside the proxy bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual maturity and interest reconciliation; replace the proxy with exact coupon cash dates when available.

assumptions.rationale: Approximate within-year interest using average principal: opening principal less the declared fraction of that year's retirement. The maturity table places most payments between winter and summer. This timing estimate affects annual interest only; all principal is paid in its contractual holding year and terminal interest is zero.
assumptions.counterevidence: Individual November and December payments differ from a midpoint approximation.
assumptions.falsifier: Exact payment dates create interest outside the jointly stressed timing and coupon bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual debt-payment reconciliation or amended terms.

assumptions.rationale: Translate future euro principal relative to the latest reported USD amounts. Downside combines dollar weakness with operating stress. Reconcile the same translation into projected outstanding principal and all affected repayments; it creates no current cash.
assumptions.counterevidence: Exchange rates can move differently and foreign operating earnings provide a partial economic hedge.
assumptions.falsifier: Translated maturity requirements fall outside these bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Material euro movement or annual debt disclosure.

assumptions.rationale: Declared nominal USD owner hurdle balances diversified profitable transactions against concentrated customers, incentive funding, intervention and short-duration guarantees. It is a business-specific judgment, not a market-derived default. Keep the rate constant across scenarios because operating deterioration and funding failure are executed in cash flows.
assumptions.counterevidence: Network resilience could justify less; systemic guarantees could require more or extinguish equity.
assumptions.falsifier: Interoperability economics erode or survival requires unavailable financing.

assumptions.rationale: The 2025 annual revenue bridge attributes approximately three percentage points of services growth to acquisitions. Applied to USD 10,832 million of 2024 services revenue, this gives USD 324.96 million of acquired revenue contribution. The bounds recognize rounding and classification uncertainty, not undisclosed synergies.
assumptions.counterevidence: The bridge aggregates acquisitions and their partial-year comparisons; it is not a cohort profit disclosure.
assumptions.falsifier: A reconciled acquisition revenue disclosure falls outside the bounded contribution.
assumptions.review_trigger: Annual acquisition, services-growth and integration disclosures.

assumptions.rationale: Convert acquired revenue into incremental after-tax parent owner earnings after ordinary integration costs, maintenance and compensation. This estimates USD 64.992 million, USD 97.488 million and USD 129.984 million against the complete USD 2,511 million purchase-capital denominator: approximately 2.59%, 3.88% and 5.18%. No unquantified parent synergies, margin above acquired revenue, or integration-cost addback is credited. Full purchase consideration remains the equity-capital denominator; forward acquisitions receive no additional borrowing.
assumptions.counterevidence: Purchased services may have lower margins or longer integration lags; shared distribution could create benefits absent from this estimate. Reported acquisition growth does not identify marginal cash profit.
assumptions.falsifier: Subsequent acquired-business earnings, cash or impairment disclosures contradict the estimated contribution after a full integration period.
assumptions.review_trigger: Every material acquisition, annual integration review and impairment disclosure.

assumptions.rationale: The January–December 2027 commitment combines January–October from holding year 1 with November–December from holding year 2. Allocate annual operating revenue and recurring cash evenly within each holding year, giving ten-twelfths and two-twelfths. This is an explicit interpolation judgment, not a claim that holding-year and fiscal-year totals are identical. The range tests seasonality and within-year acquisition integration timing.
assumptions.counterevidence: Cross-border activity, incentive payments, litigation and acquisitions are seasonal or lumpy; annual interpolation cannot reproduce exact quarterly cash dates.
assumptions.falsifier: Comparable fiscal results differ materially because the implied within-year allocation is outside the bounds.
assumptions.review_trigger: Quarterly results and the 2027 annual cash-flow statement; replace interpolation with reported fiscal stubs as available.

normalization.conclusion: Trailing revenue, income and OCF remain USD 36,288 million, USD 16,958 million and USD 16,861 million. The USD 1,241 million recast is explicitly +5,137-2,602-2,838-193+23+675+1,039 in millions. It removes identified funding/timing before incremental customer deployment. Maintenance, compensation and outside claims remain charged once. Revenue grew 12.23% and 16.42% in 2024–2025; a consistently defined cash proxy after physical/software spending, SBC and customer-deposit inflows grew approximately 28.3% and 19.6%, while latest nine-month OCF weakened. This supports testing persistent adoption and deteriorating conversion separately, without buyback-driven operating growth.

working_capital.conclusion: Latest incentive assets of USD 11,624 million versus USD 10,401 million and the USD 649 million receivable increase support explicit customer-capital requirements. Rebates and incentive expense already reduce net revenue; the additional deployment represents cash/capital beyond that charged earning-power boundary. Capital uses the greater of matched attributed-profit funding and customer intensity. Acquired revenue receives customer capital and operating liquidity. Annual funding caps reduce expansion revenue when resources are insufficient. Existing customer assets and operating buffers are not liquidated during contraction.

maintenance_and_growth_capex.conclusion: Retain the explicit maintenance and economic-compensation deductions in owner earnings; additional bridge funding for those embedded charges remains zero. Forward organic profit attribution now matches the historical attributed incremental-return numerator. Customer and operating-liquidity floors remain independent. Acquisition returns derive from disclosed acquired revenue and bounded after-tax owner margins; the resulting approximately 2.59%–5.18% returns confer no acquisition franchise. Failed-payback spending remains charged. Expensed development is not capitalized and charged a second time.

financing_scope.conclusion: Latest unrestricted cash and gross principal still anchor the parent claim; restricted balances and customer collateral remain unavailable. Conditional early credit has an executed failure alternative and is repaid before expiry. All 25 annual bridges retain scheduled principal and declining interest without replacement borrowing. Positive organic deployment is capped in every year after compulsory uses and liquidity. Year-end liquidity comprises a nondecreasing operating target plus the following year's scheduled principal; this funds early-year maturities without full prefunding of long-dated debt. Reserve changes are retained cash movements, not additional debt repayments. No borrowed dollar is also counted as undrawn capacity.

dilution.conclusion: Use the verified September 2026 quarterly diluted denominator of 876 million shares, newer than the annual baseline and on the verified split basis. It covers participating common classes and existing dilution. Economic compensation funding is charged once inside owner earnings; no free share shrinkage or uncommitted rescue equity is assumed. There is no listing ratio and no ADR/ADS conversion.

terminal.conclusion: The owner holding period is seven years; all 25 years remain audited for funding. The compiler values later shareholder cash at the holding date and adds one sale. Debt principal and interest continue through their original maturities, then terminate before continuing equity capitalization. Terminal owner earnings retain maintenance, SBC, ordinary taxes and outside claims before growth. Continuation return equals total incremental parent owner earnings divided by complete organic, acquisition and incremental operating-liquidity capital. It no longer takes a minimum against an attributed organic return with a different numerator. Release of a next-year principal reserve is excluded from this growth-capital calibration. No separate retained-cash or portfolio recovery is added.

method_selection.conclusion: Consolidated operating DCF fits interdependent network and services claims. Sum-of-parts lacks separable distributable earnings and investment boundaries. Settlement guarantees require dated funding analysis without treating Mastercard as an account-holder lender. NAV would omit franchise earnings or double count supporting assets.

scenario_coherence.conclusion: Low combines contraction, lasting margin damage, weak conversion, lower deployment returns, higher maintenance, euro obligations and early legal/customer demands. The early waterfall executes failure when timely resources are unavailable. Every annual positive-growth forecast is additionally limited by internal resources after debt, acquisitions and liquidity; weaker investment returns cannot demand unavailable capital while leaving revenue unchanged. Renewal deterioration jointly stresses the recast, conversion, customer funding and capital returns on a surviving path. Fast erosion and materially longer distribution persistence operate over the full explicit projection, while the equity hurdle remains constant across cases.

components.claim_scope: Prospective distributions and one continuing-equity realization for legacy Mastercard parent common shareholders, per verified diluted common share, conditional on meeting the early payment deadline.
components.scope_reconciliation: Cash generation is normalized parent owner earnings after maintenance, economic SBC, ordinary taxes, outside claims and financing costs, before separately paid organic growth and acquisitions. Reported income and OCF provide its numerical boundary; additional maintenance/SBC bridge funding remains zero because those costs are embedded. Historical organic attribution also applies to the forward incremental-profit numerator. Customer capital remains an independent floor. In every projected year, bp/br/fg cap positive installed growth using opening cash and cash at the preceding revenue base, after current financing costs, scheduled principal, acquisition consideration, acquired-customer funding, the existing operating buffer and next-year principal reservation. The calculation does not depend on earnings from proposed positive growth. funding_intensity also reserves liquidity for achieved growth; acquired liquidity is reserved separately. Unfunded expansion and its revenue disappear together; negative operating shocks remain intact. Discretionary organic deployment occurs as internally generated cash becomes available, after creditor needs; distributions occur after annual obligations and reserve replenishment. At year-end, cash includes the nondecreasing operating target plus the following year's scheduled principal, supporting early-year maturities without replacement notes. Principal-reserve changes enter retained cash, and actual repayment enters net financing once. The separate early waterfall retains conditional committed borrowing and permanent legacy-common loss on a missed demand. Later corporate obligations remain intact, emergency credit is repaid before expiry, and interest ends with principal retirement. Acquisitions remain paid even when payoff fails. Fiscal-2027 commitments combine ten-twelfths of holding year 1 and two-twelfths of year 2 under an explicit within-year interpolation judgment, including the delayed acquired contribution and weighted financing costs. OCF reconstruction precedes physical/software capital and economic SBC funding, retains ordinary renewal/legal expense, and deducts incremental customer cash. Exceptional early legal/settlement payments are dated November 2026 and therefore excluded from fiscal-2027 payments; no tax recovery is credited. No new notes, owner rescue, free share shrinkage, separate cash/NAV uplift or second terminal debt deduction is assumed.

terminal.rationale: The seven-year ownership realization transfers all remaining reconciled shareholder cash; the 25-year projection continues through the final existing note and contains no duplicate exit. Desired competitive growth now fades across the complete explicit schedule: base approaches maturity around year 18, while high retains approximately 4.6% desired growth in year 25, subject to annual capital availability. No additional privileged runway is appended afterward. Terminal owner earnings retain maintenance, compensation, ordinary taxes and outside claims, excluding the final temporary interest charge after all principal retires. Incremental return uses total incremental owner earnings, including installed gains and the delayed acquired contribution, divided by all explicit organic/acquisition capital and incremental operating liquidity. The next-year principal reserve is financing liquidity, excluded from this return denominator. The compiler charges mature growth reinvestment and creates the sole realization. Failed early common ownership receives none.

earning_power.assessment: The latest report preserves the operating-DCF framework but challenges cash conversion: earnings rose while nine-month OCF fell. Retain the reported trailing income/OCF bridge and explicit numerical recast, with ordinary maintenance, compensation and renewal expense charged once. Historical aggregate revenue and cash growth support a materially longer persistence range; annual internal-capital limits determine achieved growth rather than asserting that every desired opportunity can be financed.

reinvestment.assessment: Separate installed gains, newly funded organic returns and acquired returns. The corrected acquired numerator derives from approximately USD 324.96 million of disclosed acquired-revenue contribution times a bounded 20%–40% owner margin, with no unsupported synergies. Organic historical attribution also applies forward before dividing by the organic return; customer and liquidity floors remain independently funded. Each year's attainable growth falls when internally available capital is insufficient. Continuation uses total incremental owner earnings over complete funded capital, excluding debt-interest savings and principal-reserve releases.

competitive_response.assessment: Net revenue grew 12.23% and 16.42% in 2024–2025. Current currency-neutral network/services growth and their revenue mix imply approximately 12.7%, supporting base desired growth near 10%–11% and a persistent high path. Faster incentives, slowing transaction/cross-border growth, local routing and account-based competitors oppose automatic extrapolation. Base fade extends to approximately year 18; high remains above mature growth in year 25. Rapid erosion and slower fade are distinct executable alternatives, independent of the holding date and constrained by funded deployment.

customer_value.assessment: Interoperability, security and acceptance create customer value, but merchant acceptance costs and issuer rewards constrain pricing. Mastercard receives no interchange revenue. Faster incentive growth contradicts unrestricted pricing power. Customer funding and margin concessions reduce owner distributions.

capital_allocation.assessment: Maintain ordinary replacement technology, compensation and renewals in owner earnings, separately fund organic deployment and acquisitions, then retain operating cash and the next year's principal before payouts. Forward organic attribution matches the historical return numerator; lower returns can reduce achieved growth instead of forcing financing. Acquisition payoff is deliberately unattractive on the disclosed calibration and can fail completely while consideration remains paid. Constant shares and pro-rata distributions provide no free buyback accretion.

financing_survival.assessment: Early settlement/legal payments exclude unearned annual receipts and use conditional, capped committed credit. The existing failure waterfall extinguishes common participation without cancelling corporate obligations. For every later year, internal deployment is capped after current financing, scheduled principal, acquisitions, customer funding, operating cash and next-year principal. These cash reserves fund subsequent early-year maturities before discretionary expansion or distributions. No later facility renewal, new note issuance or owner rescue is assumed; final principal and interest remain reconciled through 2051.

inflation.assessment: All forecasts and the hurdle remain nominal USD. Pricing/payment amounts, wages, incentives and replacement costs enter revenue, margins and capital requirements consistently. Operating liquidity rises with achieved revenue. Euro translation affects outstanding principal and repayments together. No macro uplift or automatic working-capital recovery is credited, and financial principal reserves remain distinct from operating investment.

realization.assessment: Use a seven-year owner holding period with all subsequent obligations and shareholder proceeds valued at that date by the compiler. Preserve the full 25-year contractual funding schedule, declining interest and final debt-free continuation. Competitive duration is independently calibrated and tested; no horizon is chosen to improve IRR. Total incremental equity returns reconcile complete funded capital, while retained operating cash, investments and principal reserves receive no duplicate realization.

failure_states.rationale: Settlement exposure generally lasts days. Aggregate stress legal demands, settlement losses and imminent obligations before prospective annual receipts. Timely borrowing is capped and conditional. If resources are insufficient at the deadline, legacy common participation is permanently extinguished. Unpaid demands remain in year-1 residual claims and incur an explicit financing allowance; they are not scaled away with ownership.
failure_states.payment_timing: Stress deadline approximately nine days after underwriting, including the November 9 prior-record dividend and reservation of November note principal. Accelerated legal collection is an assumption, not a reported court timetable. Facility funds must arrive before this deadline.

hypotheses.explanation: Installed interoperability and shared services distribution generate attractive incremental owner earnings after customer funding, replacement technology and capability purchases.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Incentive assets and goodwill increased while recent OCF declined despite greater income.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Reported fiscal-2027 revenue and OCF, using the declared calendar interpolation, and subsequent owner cash rise relative to cumulative funded customer, expansion, acquisition and operating-liquidity capital. Activity and services retain growth without incentives absorbing the incremental customer value.

hypotheses.explanation: Customer funding and acquisitions produce revenue with weaker or later cash payback than installed-network margins suggest.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Margins improved and recent annual cash generation grew materially.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Post-integration acquired revenue and owner cash fail to support the revised approximately 2.59%–5.18% full-consideration return, while acquisitions and customer deployment continue consuming cash. Compare the fiscal-2027 OCF commitment with the revenue commitment; revenue growth alone cannot validate payback.

hypotheses.explanation: Acceptance costs, issuer bargaining and competing rails constrain pricing and reduce returns on customer deployment.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Network and services revenue continue growing and several legal matters have resolved.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: Activity rises while net revenue per activity falls, customer capital increases and after-tax margins fail to recover.

hypotheses.explanation: Correlated settlement and legal demands can exceed cash and timely borrowing before profitable annual operations replenish resources.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Historical settlement losses are low, credit is committed and recent issuance demonstrates access.
hypotheses.discriminating_observation: A dated demand exceeds cash plus executable borrowing before its deadline, or a valid timely facility draw demonstrably closes the gap.

structural_tests.rationale: Combine operating contraction, weaker conversion, higher maintenance and customer failures with unavailable timely credit and no owner rescue. Legal cash of USD 5 billion plus settlement severity of 5% and imminent obligations exceed opening usable cash. The early waterfall executes unpaid demands and permanent legacy common loss; later corporate cash pays remaining claims. All subsequent existing principal still retires without replacement financing.

Adverse demands coincide with timely committed access. Borrowing must arrive before the early deadline, remain within capacity, incur interest and be repaid by year 3 before later payouts. No replacement notes are available at any point.

Cash pays all early senior demands without facility access but falls below the operating target. Ownership and revenue remain intact; subsequent cash is retained and distributions fall while scheduled maturities are paid internally.

Keep replacement note issuance unavailable through March 2051 and no facility renewal beyond its disclosed term. Existing principal retires on its schedule with declining interest. Reserve only the following year's maturity alongside operating liquidity, cap expansion to internally available capital in every year, and reduce payouts before financing requirements. The seven-year sale transfers this entire remaining claim; it does not restore refinancing access or erase later payments.

Preserve every annual acquisition purchase and the BVNK contingency while removing all forward-vintage contributions. Customer funding attached solely to nonexistent acquired revenue disappears, but purchase consideration remains spent. Lower incremental earnings relative to total deployed capital also reduces the continuation return.

Jointly lower the cash recast and conversion, increase customer funding and maintenance, and reduce attributed organic returns. Preserve the same annual acquisition cash and complete debt schedule. Historical attribution now also applies to forward profit; each year's fg node reduces achieved expansion and the related capital outlay when internal resources cannot fund desired growth. Payouts follow operating liquidity and the following year's principal reserve. This is a surviving, internally financed renewal path rather than unchanged growth financed by an unexplained shortfall.

Routing intervention and renewal concessions eliminate elevated desired growth after recovery. Set subsequent opportunity to mature growth immediately while retaining funded customer requirements, acquisitions, compensation, operating liquidity and every debt maturity. Growth can fall further when internal funding binds; the constant hurdle does not disguise the operating change.

Test adoption and shared services distribution persisting near recent measured growth: desired subsequent growth begins at 14% and fades only 0.2 percentage points annually, retaining approximately 9.8% in year 25. This is materially longer persistence than base, not duplicated mature years. All acquisitions, customer capital, replacement costs, operating liquidity and existing principal remain funded; annual internal resources can constrain achieved growth. Terminal growth and the equity hurdle remain unchanged.

base_contract.holding_horizon_rationale: Seven years permits observation of customer renewals, several software replacement cycles and acquired-capability payback. This ownership horizon is independent of the final debt maturity. Retain all 25 projected years and their obligations; the compiler values the remaining shareholder claim at year 7 using the same equity hurdle and creates one sale.

value.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed January 2028 USD 750 million and February 2028 USD 500 million maturities. December 2027 euro principal remains separately translated through m2_fx. This disaggregation changes neither total principal nor its annual payment.
value.counterevidence: Contractual amendments could change principal or timing.
value.falsifier: The disclosed January or February maturity is amended.
value.review_trigger: Each debt amendment and annual maturity reconciliation.

value.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed March 2028 USD notes: 300 million floating, 450 million fixed and 750 million fixed. The remaining USD 1,750 million matures in June. Preserve the existing annual USD 4,500 million payment.
value.counterevidence: Contractual amendments could change payment dates or amounts.
value.falsifier: The disclosed March maturity sum changes.
value.review_trigger: Each debt amendment and annual maturity reconciliation.

value.rationale: By the March 2028 payments, require cumulative net internal cash from November 2027 to equal at least 10% of the conservative year-2 cash envelope. Assume cumulative net cash before March is nonnegative; reserve all December, January and February principal without crediting receipts. The envelope excludes profits from proposed organic expansion and deducts full desired organic funding, acquisitions, acquired-customer capital, incremental acquired operating liquidity, outside claims, note interest and a full opening-draw financing allowance. Weekly customer billing and ordinarily short payment terms support periodic collection. Historical January–March OCF represented approximately 16.0%, 11.3% and 13.5% of annual OCF in 2023–2025. Those observations support a deliberately lower 7.5% stress bound over this longer collection window, but do not establish future net receipt timing.
value.counterevidence: Quarterly OCF is not cash after investment. Incentive renewals, legal payments, taxes and customer failures can cluster; weekly billing does not guarantee collection. The envelope and payment priority therefore require explicit underwriting judgments.
value.falsifier: Cumulative net internal cash is negative before March or falls below the stressed fraction by a maturity deadline despite deferring discretionary deployment and payouts.
value.review_trigger: Every quarterly cash and incentive disclosure; immediately review collection disruption, accelerated commitments or payment-date changes. Replace interpolation with dated balances and receipts as available.

value.rationale: By June 2028 require at least 40% of the same conservative annual net cash envelope to have accumulated over November–June. This allows substantial receipt backloading relative to the elapsed eight months. The company bills customers periodically and generated positive first-half OCF in every displayed recent year. Deduct full desired annual deployment and fixed modeled cash uses in the envelope before applying the fraction; do not credit additional borrowing or positive-growth earnings. Stress the fraction jointly with unavailable credit and the intermediate operating squeeze.
value.counterevidence: Historical first-half OCF does not reveal daily net cash after acquisitions and customer funding. Concentrated renewal payments or collection disruption could make even the 35% stress bound too favorable.
value.falsifier: Net cash accumulated by June falls below the stressed envelope fraction after applying creditor-first deployment sequencing.
value.review_trigger: Quarterly cash conversion, incentive payment schedules and acquisition commitments; review immediately if investment cannot be deferred behind maturity payments.

edits.value: The operating minimum is half the latest unrestricted cash, rising with achieved revenue and never automatically declining with contraction. A separate payout and growth-allocation target adds the following year's entire scheduled principal. That full-year prefunding target is discretionary; it is neither an additional current debt payment nor the operating minimum. For the initial intermediate squeeze, an explicit dated minimum additionally reserves December–February principal without receipt credit and March/June cumulative principal net of bounded internal receipts. Preserve every actual maturity payment, acquisition charge and financing cost. Discretionary deployment follows creditor payments and operating liquidity; distributions remain residual.

Actual operating cash requirements may exceed the estimate. A shortfall against the full-year prefunding target can be harmless only when dated internal receipts cover subsequent maturities while preserving operating cash; annual profitability alone does not demonstrate this.
Usable cash falls below the operating minimum, or dated resources cannot meet a contractual payment after discretionary deployment and payouts have been deferred.
Quarterly liquidity and cash conversion, settlement stress, regulatory requirements, payment-date changes and failure of either receipt-timing commitment.

Latest carrying debt of USD 23,938 million reconciles to gross principal of USD 24,081 million through discounts, costs and hedge adjustments. Preserve every maturity and declining-interest node through March 2051. Full next-year principal remains a discretionary prefunding target in growth allocation and payouts. The hard operating minimum is distinct; the initial stressed shortfall additionally requires an explicit December–June funding envelope. Target retention and actual repayment remain separate cash movements. Emergency credit stays conditional, capped, priced and repaid by year 3; undrawn capacity is never borrowed cash.

Cash generation remains normalized parent owner earnings after maintenance, economic SBC, ordinary taxes, outside claims and financing costs, before separately paid organic growth and acquisitions. Reported income and OCF establish the numerical boundary; additional maintenance/SBC bridge funding stays zero because those costs are embedded. Historical organic attribution applies to forward incremental profit, and customer capital remains an independent floor. Annual bp/br/fg constraints retain the existing full next-year principal prefunding target when allocating expansion and payouts. This target is discretionary and is not an additional current creditor payment. The operating minimum remains nondecreasing with achieved revenue. The initial intermediate squeeze can miss full prefunding while preserving operations and paying creditors. Its additional dated_floor1 reserves December 2027, January 2028 and February 2028 principal without receipt credit, plus any larger March or June cumulative principal requirement after bounded internal receipts. timing_y2_net excludes proposed organic-growth earnings and deducts full desired organic capital and liquidity, acquisitions, acquired-customer capital and liquidity, outside claims, note interest and financing on the entire opening emergency draw. Its deductions are a timing envelope, not additional annual cash charges. Net receipts must remain nonnegative before March, reach the declared fraction by March and the larger fraction by June. Discretionary deployment is paced behind dated payments and operating liquidity; annual investment charges and contributions remain unchanged. Later payout targets continue retaining complete next-year principal, and no later shortfall is excused by this distinction. The early creditor waterfall still uses only timely cash and eligible committed borrowing; actual missed demands permanently extinguish legacy common participation without cancelling corporate obligations. All principal and declining interest remain projected through 2051, with emergency credit repaid before expiry. Acquisition consideration remains paid when payoff fails. Fiscal-2027 commitments retain their explicit calendar interpolation and cash reconstruction. Constant shares receive no free repurchase accretion. No new borrowing, owner rescue, reserve recovery, duplicate interest saving, separate cash uplift or second exit is introduced.

Retain latest unrestricted cash, restricted-resource exclusions, conditional credit and all 25 years of actual principal and interest. Distinguish oper_floor operating requirements from floor full-next-year prefunding targets used by expansion and distributions. The intermediate low path closes year 1 with approximately USD 8.422 billion, above USD 5.0735 billion operating cash but below the USD 10.61885 billion full prefunding target. Its approximately USD 3.348 billion excess operating cash covers USD 2.29535 billion of December–February principal without receipts. March cumulative principal is USD 3.79535 billion and June cumulative principal USD 5.54535 billion. The additional dated minimum offsets these payments only with explicitly bounded internal receipts, using an envelope that excludes organic-growth earnings and deducts full desired deployment and financing costs. The March/June assumptions and tighter joint stress make timing reviewable. Annual profitability alone is insufficient. Existing full prefunding targets, actual debt payments, financing scope and shareholder cash flows remain unchanged.

Preserve correlated operating contraction, margin damage, conversion weakness, customer funding, euro obligations and early legal/settlement demands. Actual early creditor failure still extinguishes common equity. The intermediate squeeze pays immediate claims but misses a discretionary full-year prefunding target; it now must satisfy an additional dated December–June liquidity minimum rather than merely passing an annual operating-cash test. A tighter receipt-backloading alternative retains unavailable credit and the same adverse demands. Maintenance, compensation, acquisitions, organic funding, maturity payments and all later targets remain charged. No fractional ownership loss, fictitious creditor default, automatic refinancing or extra capital source closes the target gap.

The operator correctly distinguishes full-year prefunding from actual debt due, but replacing every minimum with operating cash alone leaves receipt timing implicit. Add a stronger dated minimum for the sole initial target shortfall. December–February principal is fully covered without receipts; March and June cumulative payments receive only declared fractions of a conservative internally generated cash envelope. Weekly billing, short ordinary payment terms and positive historical quarterly cash generation support periodic receipts, while incentive, tax and acquisition lumpiness remain counterevidence. The envelope excludes prospective organic-growth earnings and deducts full desired deployment, acquisitions and financing costs. Deployment follows creditor needs; distributions retain the existing larger prefunding targets. All later principal, interest and facility repayment remain executable through 2051. Genuine early unpaid demands still cause permanent common loss.

Maintain replacement technology, compensation and renewals in owner earnings; separately fund organic deployment and acquisitions. Full next-year principal remains the preferred retention target before expansion and distributions, distinct from operating liquidity and actual payments. Initial stressed under-prefunding is permitted only within the dated receipt envelope, with discretionary spending paced behind creditors. The envelope deducts desired investment for timing analysis without charging it again in annual bridges. Acquisition failure still preserves purchase spending; constant shares and pro-rata distributions create no free buyback accretion.

Preserve the USD 3 billion legal demand, 3% settlement severity and unavailable facility. Immediate creditors are paid; no fractional ownership loss occurs. In low, year-1 cash is approximately USD 8.422 billion against USD 5.0735 billion operating cash. The full USD 10.61885 billion prefunding target is missed, but it is not a debt due that year. Require dated_floor1: reserve all December–February principal without receipts and preserve operating cash through March and June using only the declared conservative internal-receipt fractions. Annual investment, principal, interest and payout rules remain intact. Failure of this timing judgment requires revising the path, not invoking annual profits as funding.

value.rationale: Retain the intermediate legal/customer shock and unavailable facility while reducing cumulative usable net receipts to 7.5% of the conservative annual envelope by March and 35% by June. Credit no receipts toward December–February principal. This tests substantial collection backloading jointly with funding closure; the hard dated minimum must preserve operating liquidity at each maturity checkpoint. Keep every annual acquisition, compensation, maintenance and principal charge, and defer discretionary deployment behind dated payments. No rescue capital or facility renewal is available.

edits.value: Keep replacement issuance unavailable through March 2051 and assume no facility renewal. Existing principal retires on schedule with declining interest. Full next-year principal remains a discretionary prefunding target in annual growth allocation and payouts, separate from the operating minimum; the initial shortfall additionally faces dated December–June funding checks. Preserve all later targets, maturity payments and investment constraints. The seven-year sale transfers the entire remaining claim and restores no financing access.

Compare each actual payment deadline with usable opening cash and cash collected before that deadline. Distinguish a missed contractual payment from a shortfall against discretionary full-year prefunding. In the intermediate squeeze, test nonnegative pre-March net receipts and the March/June envelope fractions after creditor-first deployment sequencing. A valid timely facility draw can close a gap only when the facility-access assumption permits it.
